newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices gain, optimism grows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices gain, optimism grows.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices gained from 3/8 to a 1/4 of a point late Tuesday, and while they lagged U.S. Treasuries, optimism over the market's near-term direction prompted some dealers to mark-up planned offerings.
"I'm seeing some sales for tomorrow with scales that are pretty stiff," said a trader, citing competitive sales.
Though no details were disclosed, the trader explained that issuers evidently believe prices will not only hold their recent strength, but add to their gains.
"I think there's a 'buy now and sell later' mentality."

The yield on the cash 30-year Treasury fell to 6.44 percent, its lowest level since March 6, amid some optimism that bi-partisanship cooperation could lead to a resolution on a balanced budget, analysts said.

Traders also cited the dollar's ability to hold gains versus the Swiss franc, mark and yen, and rising confidence that Treasuries will keep rising. "It's a continuing trend and the dollar gave people an excuse to buy," one said.
Smaller supplies of municipal bonds, however, helped prevent them from matching the Treasuries' climb.
"It's probably because there are not a lot of bonds to trade around," a trader said. The Standard & Poor's Blue List stood at $1.1 billion, a level considered moderate.
A steep fall-off in the amount of new issues slated for sale could help prop prices up over a slightly longer time frame.
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $819 million in 30 offerings for Wednesday Nov 13.
Competitive sales total $245 million in 18 offerings. The largest competitive issue is a $90 million Boston, Mass., general obligation issue at 1100 EST.
Negotiated sales total $573 million in 12 offerings. The largest issue is a $161 State of Connecticut issue through Merrill Lynch & Co.
This is a marked contrast to mid- to late-October, when the calenders totaled $4 billion to $5 billion.
And next week's calender also is expected to be fairly light.
"There's not a lot of selling by customers, not a lot of calender this week or next, so the technicals favor the market," a trader said.
Much of the day's activity was concentrated in bonds issued by New York City, as it last week sold $834 million of tax-exempt general obligation bonds.
"There were balances around in city GOs that were being traded around and cleaned up," a trader said.
The city's paper rose about 1/4 of a point, he added.
Actively quoted issues included Alambama Water Pollution Control Authority Revolving Fund of August 2020, which were bid at 5.71 percent NET, and pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon.
And Metropolitan Pier & Exposition Authority Illinios Dedicated State Tax Revenue Refunding of June 2027, which carry a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.67 percent NET.
No quotes were available from Monday because it was the U.S. Veteran's Day holiday.
December municipal bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade gained 17 ticks to 117-5/32, while December Treasuries climbed 27 ticks to 114-29/32. The MOB spread narrowed slightly to plus 72 ticks.
--Joan Gralla, 212-859-1654
